_doc: One file per place; see places_build.py. Amounts in Swiss francs. The debt component, history and facts are refreshed by pipeline/fetch_switzerland.py from the Federal Finance Administration's quarterly GFS workbooks; edit wording here, not numbers.
name: Switzerland
title: Switzerland Debt Clock: Live Federal Gross Debt, Official Data
headline: federal gross debt
subject: The Swiss Confederation (federal government)
sum_note: Swiss Confederation gross debt (Bruttoschulden) in the Federal Finance Administration's quarterly GFS statistics (SDDS Plus), quarter-end. Gross, federal government only; includes non-borrowing liabilities such as accounts payable.
scope_note: This is the Federal Finance Administration's "Bruttoschulden Bund" from its quarterly government finance statistics (GFS), as reported for the IMF's SDDS Plus: all the Confederation's financial liabilities except gold and special drawing rights. Besides deposits, debt securities and loans, GFS counts insurance and pension liabilities and other accounts payable, which is why this is larger than the amount the Confederation has actually borrowed; that borrowed part is shown below as a fact. Cantons, municipalities and the social insurance funds are not in it; the wider general government total is shown as a second fact. Figures are in Swiss francs and are not reduced by any assets.
trend_why: We use the latest twelve months rather than the last quarter because changes between single reporting dates swing with the issuance calendar and short-term borrowing.
legend: Switzerland's federal debt is reported quarterly, at quarter-end. The live number is a straight-line projection between official quarter-end figures, shown here next to them.
cadence: Quarterly. The Federal Finance Administration publishes each quarter-end figure about three months after the quarter ends.
after_text: , about three months after each quarter-end
next_update: The Q3 2026 quarter-end figure is expected from the Federal Finance Administration roughly three months after the quarter ends; this page re-bases to it automatically on the next daily build after it appears.

notes: Why this measure: Bruttoschulden is the Federal Finance Administration's own gross debt line in the quarterly GFS statistics it reports to the IMF, the closest official match to the US clock's gross total. Its breakdown by instrument adds up to the headline and the fetcher checks that.

Why it is larger than borrowing: the GFS gross debt counts all liabilities except gold and SDRs, including insurance and pension liabilities and other accounts payable. The money actually borrowed is shown as a fact.

The debt brake: Switzerland's constitutional debt brake works on the federal budget balance, not on this stock measure. The Federal Finance Administration publishes other debt figures on a national accounting basis that differ from this GFS series.
The franc: the World Debt Clock converts Swiss francs to US dollars at the ECB's daily reference rate for CHF.
